title: Jarl: new refuses a text that holds a tag named after one of its own fields, and its reply lists what was parsed and what was left empty, with the command that fills each
claim: A caller whose tool call carried every field inside the What parameter got tickets with the default priority, no tags and empty Why and Acceptance on every call (about 30 in one session), and could not tell from the reply that anything was wrong, because the reply is only the number and the file.
evidence: cmdNew writes each flag into its own place and reads nothing out of a text value (JarlSkill/skills/jarl/scripts/jarl-lib.mjs:955), so the tags in the What text came from the calling side; the reply is 'filed NNN · file' (jarl.mjs:474 at 67615e6); a field report from a private deployment of 6.1.0, section 3.1 and 3.6 (source.md). Not reproduced in this pass.
proposal: new and body refuse a What, Why or section text that holds an opening or closing tag named what, why, acceptance, prio, tags, files or kind, naming the field and saying to pass it as its own parameter. The reply of new lists the parsed priority, tier, tags, the number of acceptance lines and the lengths of What and Why, and the fields left empty (Why, Acceptance, Files, After, Where, Found by), each with the command that fills it (body, files, after). Tests: all fields given, each parsed into its section or header; a What carrying <why>...</why> refused with the field named; the reply of a bare new names every empty field. First step: reproduce the report's call on a scratch loop. 6.2.0.

title: Jarl: new run from a linked worktree of a committed loop refuses and names the main checkout, and takes the highest number over the main checkout and every linked worktree
claim: Two workers that filed tickets inside their own worktrees of a committed loop each got a number already used in the main checkout, so two pairs of tickets shared a number and were renumbered by hand.
evidence: cmdNew takes the next number from the files of the loop it was given, the highest plus one (JarlSkill/skills/jarl/scripts/jarl-lib.mjs:992); in the committed mode a worktree holds only the copy it was cut with (SKILL.md:121-124); a field report from a private deployment of 6.1.0, section 3.2 (source.md). Read from the code, not reproduced.
proposal: When the root given to new is a linked worktree of a repository whose main checkout holds the same loop, new refuses and names the main checkout as the root to pass. Where it does run, the number is the highest over the main checkout and every linked worktree of the repository (git worktree list), read-only, so a lagging copy cannot hand out a used number. No counter file: the issue files stay the only source. Tests: a committed loop with a worktree that lags by two issues, new from the worktree refused; new on the main checkout with a worktree that holds a higher number takes the higher one plus one. 6.2.0.

title: Jarl: the reply of review names the next step (approved: merge, then set done with evidence; changes: a round), so a reviewer's verdict does not leave the coordinator guessing who closes
claim: After twelve approves and five sends-back the tickets stayed open and in-progress in the list, and nothing said that the next step was a merge and then a move to done, by whom, with which command.
evidence: cmdReview returns the verdict, the reviewer's kind, the severities and the acceptance, and nothing about what follows (JarlSkill/skills/jarl/scripts/jarl-lib.mjs:2113-2142); the flow is in SKILL.md only; a field report from a private deployment of 6.1.0, section 3.4 (source.md). The view 'approved, not closed' is issue 283 and is not repeated here.
proposal: The reply of an approve carries one line naming the next step: the merger merges and records it with merged, then set <id> done with the evidence rows; a worker never closes. The reply of changes names the round (round <id>) and the worker to be raised again. A coordinator's approve on a code issue keeps its existing note. Tests: the line is present on approve and on changes, and absent from neither the CLI nor the MCP reply. 6.2.0.

title: Jarl: check notes a branch that carries commits and is leased by no issue (work done without a ticket), as a note that does not change ok
claim: Nothing in Jarl notices a change made before its ticket was filed, or never ticketed; a repository whose rule is that everything is ticketed enforces it by hand.
evidence: check reads the changed files and the tests of the branch it is given and never asks whether an issue holds a lease or a Branch on it (JarlSkill/skills/jarl/scripts/jarl-lib.mjs:2280); a field report from a private deployment of 6.1.0, section 3.6 and request 7 (source.md).
proposal: check --branch lists, as one item that never changes ok (as issue 289 does for loop numbers on added lines), a branch with commits beyond the base to which no issue's Branch or lease points, naming the branch and the commit count. Tests: a branch with a lease gives no item; a branch with commits and no issue gives one; an empty branch gives none. 6.2.0.

title: Jarl: help and SKILL.md carry the recipe for many workers in worktrees (which mode, who commits .jarl, who files tickets, what in-progress means)
claim: A coordinator of about five parallel workers in worktrees did not find the three decisions the skill already makes (the default mode keeps the loop out of git and every call takes the main checkout as root; the merger is the only one who commits a committed loop; in-progress is the lease), and so reported as defects what is the design: an uncommitted loop, a shared log.md, a ticket that stays in-progress after an approve, a list it did not know how to filter.
evidence: SKILL.md:20-24 (modes), :184 (the lease), :402-409 (worker rules) hold them; help prints each command's usage and nothing on a worktree workflow (jarl.mjs:75-115, :229); jarl-lib.mjs:1109-1114 hides finished work from list by default and filters by status, kind, tag, prio, grep and match; a field report from a private deployment of 6.1.0, sections 3.3, 3.4, 3.5 and 4 (source.md). Related: issue 250 (a chapter on a loop that drives several repositories).
proposal: help ends with a short workflow section (or help workflow): for a session with parallel workers, the default mode with root set to the main checkout on every call; who commits .jarl/ (the merger, never a worker) in the committed mode; who files tickets (the coordinator, or a worker with root set to the main checkout); in-progress means held by a worker; list hides finished work and filters by tag, status, priority and text. The same text enters SKILL.md where it is missing. Tests: help's last section names the four points. 6.2.0.
